{{Dialogue|Blue|<nowiki></nowiki>''We'' got intel that says that your admiral is looking for weapons. We got fifty cases of Rawk V99 blasters to sell or trade.|R2-D2|BLOODLE DEET!|Antilles|Rawk-made? The Admiral&hellip; ''might'' be interested. Why don't we go ''talk''?|attr=Deliah Blue, R2-D2, and Ona Antilles|src=<ref name="Legacy 49" />}}
The '''Rawk V99 blaster''' was a type of [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] created by the [[Technician/Legends|mechanic]] "[[Bantha/Legends|Bantha]]" [[Rawk]], whose reputation caused the weapon to be considered of worth. In [[138 ABY]], during the [[Second Galactic Civil War]], Rawk's nephew [[Cade Skywalker]] was in possession of fifty cases of Rawk V99 blasters. When he [[Mission to Utapau (Second Imperial Civil War)|traveled]] to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Utapau/Legends|Utapau]] to [[Assassin/Legends|assassinate]] the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] [[Vul Isen]]&mdash;who was in turn trying to [[Death/Legends|kill]] [[Galactic Alliance Remnant]] [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Gar Stazi]]&mdash;Skywalker's crew met with Stazi and offered to sell him the blasters. While Skywalker [[Hunting/Legends|hunted]] Isen, his crew negotiated prices with Stazi and simultaneously kept an [[Eye/Legends|eye]] out for potential assassins targeting the Admiral.

==Description==
{{Quote|&mdash;A fine offer, no doubt, but we were thinking of a slightly ''different'' number&hellip;''"<br />"''Mind telling us what that number is? ''Gfersh!'' You're haggling like junk dealers!|Deliah Blue and Ona Antilles, negotiating the price of Rawk V99 blasters|<ref name="Legacy 50">[[Legacy (2006) 50|''Legacy'' (2006) 50]]</ref>}}
The Rawk V99 [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] was a type of blaster weapon. It was designed by "[[Bantha/Legends|Bantha]]" [[Rawk]],<ref name="Legacy 49" /> a [[Technician/Legends|mechanic]] who ran a business creating and modifying weapons for those in need of reliable armament.<ref name="Legacy 0.5">[[Star Wars: Legacy (2006) 0½|''Star Wars: Legacy'' (2006) 0½]]</ref> Rawk's favorable reputation preceded the weapon when it was for sale, and its price was negotiable when being traded on the [[Black market/Legends|black market]].<ref name="Legacy 49" />

==History==
{{Quote|Don't worry, Ona. ''Cheeka'', I got a deal the Admiral's gonna love!|Jariah Syn, on the sale of Rawk V99 blasters|<ref name="Legacy 49" />}}
[[File:Rawksignal.jpg|thumb|right|275px|R2-D2 displays the "Rawk signal" to Ona Antilles as proof of the legitimacy of the ''Mynock''{{'s}} Rawk V99 blasters.]]
[[Cade Skywalker]], a [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]]<ref name="Legacy 0.5" /> and the nephew of Rawk,<ref name="Legacy 24">[[Legacy (2006) 24|''Legacy'' (2006) 24]]</ref> possessed fifty cases of Rawk V99 blasters aboard his [[Starship/Legends|starship]], the [[Mynock (Helot-class)|''Mynock'']], during the [[Second Imperial Civil War]]<ref name="Legacy 49" /> in [[138 ABY]].<ref name="Extremes Trade">Although the [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] [[Legacy (2006) 49|''Legacy'' (2006) 49]] indicates that its events take place in [[137 ABY]], the more recently released [[Star Wars: Legacy Volume 10: Extremes|''Star Wars: Legacy: Extremes'' trade paperback]] dates them at [[138 ABY]].</ref> In that [[Standard year/Legends|year]], he [[Mission to Utapau (Second Imperial Civil War)|took]] the ''Mynock'' to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Utapau/Legends|Utapau]] in order to [[Assassin/Legends|assassinate]] the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] [[Vul Isen]], who intended to [[Poison/Legends|poison]] the world's [[Water/Legends|waters]] in retaliation for Utapau's harboring of [[Galactic Alliance Remnant]] [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Gar Stazi]], an enemy of the [[One Sith|Sith]]. When the ''Mynock'' made planetfall and was welcomed by Alliance representatives, the ship's co-[[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] [[Jariah Syn]], mechanic [[Deliah Blue]], and [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] informed Alliance [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Ona Antilles]] that they were interested in selling or trading their Rawk V99 blasters to Stazi. Although Antilles wished to speak to Skywalker himself, the crew's distraction allowed Skywalker and the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Wolf Sazen]] to slip away and [[Hunting/Legends|hunt]] for Isen.<ref name="Legacy 49" />

A [[Hologram/Legends|holographic]] symbol of Rawk's logo [[Holoprojector/Legends|displayed]] by R2-D2 convinced Antilles of the weapons' legitimacy and worth, and she spoke with the three crewmembers until Skywalker [[Comlink/Legends|contacted]] Syn and informed him that Isen had sent an assassin after Stazi. At that point, Syn demanded that the ''Mynock''{{'s}} crew be able to negotiate the blasters' prices with the Admiral himself.<ref name="Legacy 49" /> Antilles acquiesced, and, in Stazi's company, Syn surveyed the Admiral's entourage for would-be-traitors while Blue and R2-D2 bought Syn [[Time/Legends|time]] by dragging out the bargaining. After Syn caught and [[Death/Legends|killed]] the [[Unidentified assassin (Gar Stazi)|assassin]] and Skywalker elsewhere slew Isen, Blue and Stazi continued to haggle.<ref name="Legacy 50" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Rawk V99 blaster is mentioned in the [[Legacy (2006) 49|forty-ninth issue]] of the [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] series ''[[Star Wars: Legacy]]''. The issue was written by [[John Ostrander]], penciled by [[Jan Duursema]], and released by [[Dark Horse Comics]]<ref name="Legacy 49" /> on [[June 30]], [[2010]].<ref name="DarkHorse">{{DarkHorse|url=Comics/17-107/Star-Wars-Legacy-49---Extremes-Part-2|text=Star Wars: Legacy #49 - Extremes (Part 2)}}</ref>
